Per Court :

The applicant is seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in connection with Crime No.499/2019
registered with Ambad Police Station, Ambad for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 272,
273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 26, 26(2) (Iv), 27(2) (e) of Section 59 of the
Standards Food and Safety Act, 2006.

2.  It is alleged that on 29.11.2019, in the wee hours a vehicle being driven by the applicant was accosted and some prohibited articles like scented tobacco, Zafrani Zarda, Pan Masala etc., was found being transported in the vehicle.
The substance was seized.
The FIR was lodged 3.ABA.19.2020.odt by the Food Inspector and the crime was registered.

sentences.text: The learned advocate for the applicant submits that accepting the allegations in the FIR, since there are no allegations about the articles having been administered to anybody, provision of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not be applicable.
The rest of the offences being bailable and the Muddemal having been already recovered.
His presence behind the bar is not necessary to complete the investigation.
He is ready to cooperate the investigating officer and he may be released on bail.
4. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application.
She submits that the question whether Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would be applicable is a matter to be inquired into and decided by the trial court.
The applicant has been found in possession of those articles.
The applicant is a habitual offender.
Even earlier on two occasions he has been involved in a similar kind of offence.
There is every possibility of his indulging in similar crime and the application may be rejected.
5. I have carefully gone through the papers.

Certainly, in the absence of any allegation about the applicant having administered the Pan Masala or the Zafrani Zarda to anybody, there is a dispute as to the applicability of the provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code and that will have to be pondered upon and decided by the trial court.
6.
The Muddemal has already been seized.
The investigation can certainly be concluded without sending the applicant behind the bar and by making him available for interrogation.
True it is that the applicant appears to be a repeat offender in as much as already couple of cases of similar kind have been registered against him.
By taking necessary precaution to obviate any such possibility in future he can certainly be released on bail.
8. The application is allowed.

In the event of arrest of applicant he shall be released on bail on his executing personal recognizance for an amount of Rs.25,000/- and furnishing a solvent surety in the like amount subject to following conditions :
(a) He shall attend the concerned police station on first Monday of every month between 9 a.m. and 11 a.m., till conclusion of the trial.
(b) His involvement in any offence of similar kind hereafter shall result in automatic cancellation of his bail.
(c) He shall not tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses.
(MANGESH S. PATIL, J.) habeeb Anil S/O. Bandulal Pardeshi vs The State Of Maharashtra on 13 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189435567/
